sections.h2: County offices that handle property tax
sections.html:
Two county offices matter most. The Assessment Office sets the value your tax bill is built on. The Revenue and Tax Claim Bureau collects delinquent taxes. Both work from the Erie County Courthouse, 140 West Sixth Street, Erie, PA 16501. Appeals go to Room 104, and delinquent taxes are paid in Room 110.

The Assessment Office assesses all real estate in the county and runs the various tax programs. The Tax Claim Bureau is one of four divisions of the county Department of Finance. It collects delinquent taxes for the county, the City of Erie and the other municipalities, and the school districts, then passes the money out to each of them every month.

Local tax collectors bill current-year taxes. To learn what is due for the year of a sale, ask the tax collector for your municipality rather than the county.

File a Notice of Intention to Appeal Property Assessment with the Erie County Board of Appeals, and make sure it arrives between January 1 and August 1. Hearings run from July through October.

  • Use one form for each parcel.
  • Include the county parcel ID, the property location, your own estimate of value and the reason for the appeal.
  • List up to three comparable properties that sold recently or are listed for sale, by county index number, name and address.
  • Pay the non-refundable filing fee with a check made out to County of Erie.

County Council Ordinance No. 157 of 2007 sets the fee. The form cautions that comparable assessments are not treated as an indication of fair market value, and an exterior photograph of the property is available at the hearing.

Filing opens your property to revaluation, so the assessment can go down, go up or stay put. Weigh that before you file on a house you plan to sell soon. If a corporation owns the house, an officer signs the form. The county also has a Catastrophic Loss Appeal form for damage cases.

The Assessment Office's Documents and Forms page offers applications that change who is taxed or how much. Some matter to a seller, because a change of owner should be reported to the county once the deed is done.

  • Application for Homestead and Farmstead Exclusions
  • Application for Exemption From Erie County Real Property Taxes
  • Owner Change Form and Owner Registry Form
  • Clean and Green application, Clean and Green information and the Act 319 Notice of Conveyance
  • Mobile Home Change of Ownership Form
  • Change of Address form

Clean and Green land has its own notice at conveyance, so a buyer of a farm parcel should review that form before closing. Millage rate charts for each year back to 2011 are posted, with a revised chart for 2026. Rates differ by municipality and school district, so use the chart that matches your house.

The Tax Claim Bureau holds an upset sale online through GovEase for parcels whose taxes are at least two years delinquent. Bidders pre-register, the winning bid is paid in full by 3:30 p.m. on sale day, and parcels that do not sell can move to a later judicial sale run by a law firm.

The minimum bid is roughly the delinquent and current taxes plus municipal liens. The owner of a property headed to the judicial sale may not bid on it.

sections.h2: Stopping a sale or paying delinquent taxes
sections.html:
An owner can stop a sale. Even after a bid is made at the upset sale, the owner can pay the delinquency before the winning bidder pays the upset price, and the property is treated as if it had never been offered. Once the bidder pays in full, there is no redemption period.

Delinquent taxes are paid in Room 110 of the courthouse, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. The office is closed on county holidays. It takes cash, attorney IOLTA checks, money orders, certified checks, business or personal checks and MasterCard or Visa. Online payments carry an extra fee of usually around 3%. Interest and costs are added from time to time, so call the Bureau at 814-451-6206 for a current figure.

A stay of sale agreement works as an installment plan, but it cannot be set up online.

  • An owner named on the deed appears in person with state-issued ID or a passport.
  • The down payment is at least 25% of the most recent two years of delinquent taxes.
  • Any older unpaid taxes must be paid in full.
  • A default bars a new installment agreement for three years.

You can sell as long as the delinquent balance is paid from the proceeds or before closing. Ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff figure close to the closing date, since interest and costs keep accruing, and ask your municipality's tax collector for the amount on the current year's bill.

A house already in the sale process is harder. The owner of a property headed to the judicial or repository sale cannot bid on it, and repository sales carry no right of redemption. If your house is on a published list, talk to the Bureau about a stay of sale before you sign a contract, since that may buy time for a closing.

The buyer's side matters too. Liens, judgments and rents of record follow a property, which is why tax sale bidders are told to order a title search. A buyer's title agent will do the same on an ordinary sale and will insist that anything found is paid off. A cash buyer will still want taxes settled, so get the payoff in writing.

The median value of owner-occupied homes in Erie County is $177,000 for 2020 to 2024, and 68.1% of homes are owner-occupied. There are 110,587 households and median household income is $63,354. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,393, those without a mortgage $572, and median gross rent is $904. The county issued 243 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: When can I file an assessment appeal in Erie County?
faqs.a: Appeal forms are accepted from January 1 through August 1. Hearings run from July through October.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to appeal an Erie County assessment?
faqs.a: The non-refundable filing fee is $50.00 for the main parcel plus $10.00 for each additional parcel that makes up the property. Checks are made out to County of Erie.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent property taxes in Erie County?
faqs.a: Pay in Room 110 of the Erie County Courthouse, 140 West Sixth Street, Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. You can also pay online from the parcel's tax page, with an added fee of usually around 3%.

faqs.q: What is a stay of sale agreement in Erie County?
faqs.a: It is an installment plan that keeps a delinquent property out of a tax sale. It needs at least 25% of the last two years of delinquent taxes down, payment of all older taxes, and an owner on the deed appearing in person with photo ID.

faqs.q: Can the owner buy back a house after an Erie County upset sale?
faqs.a: Not after the sale is complete. The owner can pay the delinquency before the winning bidder pays the upset price, but once the bidder pays in full by 3:30 p.m. on sale day there is no period of redemption.
